title: Snowplow: Effective Kernel Fuzzing with a Learned White-box Test Mutator
problem: Kernel fuzzers rely on program mutation to generate test programs that explore new kernel code paths, but existing mutation heuristics are unable to navigate the complex control and data flow of kernel code to produce mutations that trigger target code locations or increase coverage, resulting in low fuzzing effectiveness.
motivation: OS kernel bugs remain a critical security concern; traditional fuzzing with manually-crafted mutation heuristics cannot keep pace with the complexity of modern kernel code and its user-space interface, leaving large regions of kernel code unexplored.
method: Snowplow trains a machine learning model to make smarter choices about how to mutate (modify) test programs. Instead of guessing randomly or following hand-written rules, the model learns from analyzing the actual kernel source code—specifically how instructions are ordered (control flow graphs) and how data moves between them (data flow). During testing, it predicts which mutations—like adding system calls, changing argument values, or restructuring the test—would most likely guide execution into untested kernel code regions. The model improves by learning from real coverage feedback showing which code actually ran.
key_novelty: Snowplow replaces hand-written mutation rules with a machine learning model that learns from kernel code which test changes will reach untested code.
contributions: Snowplow: a kernel fuzzer with a learned white-box mutation model replacing hand-crafted heuristics.
Demonstration of higher kernel code coverage and improved bug-finding compared to state-of-the-art kernel fuzzers.
A training methodology using kernel control/data flow as white-box features to predict effective mutations.

metrics.other: improved kernel code coverage and bug-finding rate vs state-of-the-art kernel fuzzers

baselines: existing kernel fuzzers with manual mutation heuristics
limitations: Not discussed; learned model requires training data from prior fuzzing runs and may not generalize across very different kernel versions.
primary_theme: learned white-box mutation for kernel fuzzing
